evidenceSelection.rule: Manual selection or first qualifying row in original computed order; never fabricated or chosen by largest effect.
evidenceSelection.strictClaims: A difference numerically equal to zero is a counterexample to always higher or always lower.
evidenceSelection.pinnedCases: Illustrate individual directions; every defined draw remains in the batch mean.
evidenceSelection.inspection: Reconstructs actual worlds from the captured scientific context; disabled if current controls describe another context.

scientificBoundaries: The always claim is separate from the original prediction about the batch mean.
An observed exception challenges always within the illustrative model; it does not cancel or make the arithmetic mean invalid.
If all defined draws match a claim, untested draws remain unknown. A matching example alone is not proof of always.
An absent category is a recorded batch result. Undefined H provides no directional evidence.
Caseboard steps guide a comparison and conclusion; they do not certify that a learner inspected or understood every organism.
These neutral-marker model outcomes do not prove real ecosystem behavior, genome-wide diversity, reproductive isolation or speciation.
The underlying simplified model, sampling and breeding rules are unchanged. No generated model rules or fabricated scientific outcomes are introduced.
